subject: Air-gapped update process — Medisphere (image signing & validation)
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medisphere.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.co
Cc: Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@secureops.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Air-gapped update process for Medisphere

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team asked for a written runbook that covers the full air-gapped update flow: artifact export, signing, transport to the air-gapped network, validation, and rollback steps. Important constraints: all signing must be auditable, private keys must remain offline (HSM or USB token), and Medisphere compliance requires SHA-256 manifests + signed digest.

Could you share a concrete, step-by-step process we can review and circulate to our auditors? Also include the list of artifacts we should expect in the bundle, and any pre-reqs for our ops engineers (e.g., required cosign/openssl versions, hardware tokens supported).

We'd like to pilot this in our staging (air-gapped lab) next week.

Best,
Anita
Security Lead — Medisphere Health

[attachment: requirements-request.pdf (21KB)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.co
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medisphere.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.co, dev_patel@redwood.co
Date: 2026-10-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped update process for Medisphere

Hi Anita — thanks for laying out the constraints.

High-level summary (we'll follow up with a detailed runbook and artifacts):
- Bundle format: OCI-style artifact tarball containing images (tarred OCI layout), a SHA-256 manifest (manifest.json.sha256), and an operator-level release metadata (release.yaml).
- Signing: We sign the release manifest with a detached JWS (RSASSA-PSS, SHA-256) produced by an offline signer. Redwood supports cosign for optional OCI image signatures; for air-gap flow we provide a detached JWS over the release manifest so you can verify before import.
- Key handling: Primary signing key should be HSM-backed or kept on an air-gapped USB smartcard. We support integrating with Yubikey PIV and PKCS#11 HSMs for offline signing.
- Transport: Signed bundle -> encrypted external media (AES-256 GCM) -> courier to air-gapped site.
- Validation: On the isolated network, operators verify the manifest signature (public key fingerprint pre-shared), verify SHA-256 checksums for each artifact, then run a dry-import to a validation namespace before promoting to production.
- Rollback: Keep previous signed bundle archived; import and validate it using the same verification steps.

I've attached a short checklist and will loop in Dev and Marissa for the technical commands and templates.

Next steps: Dev will provide the exact signing commands and a sample manifest; Marissa will outline where this fits into our Private deployment update API and telemetry hooks.

Regards,
Rishi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Looping in operational concerns and telemetry for the Private control-plane:

Notes:
- We need a unique release_id embedded in release.yaml to tie telemetry post-import back to the originating hosted run (masked) so Medisphere can assert provenance without exposing other tenant data.
- Console workflow: after remote import, the air-gapped operator hits a local validation endpoint (redwood-agent validate --release <id>) which checks signatures and returns a signed validation certificate that gets logged to the audit bucket.
- Audit logs: please include sample log entries (timestamped, signed) so compliance can map the chain-of-custody.

I'll review the sample commands and validate we can add the minimal API endpoint to our agent for the pilot.

From: dev_patel@redwood.co
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.co, marissa_cole@redwood.co, Anita Shah <anita.shah@medisphere.com>
Cc: Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@secureops.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped update process for Medisphere — signing commands & checklist

Hi all — attaching a compact, reproducible set of steps we've validated in our internal air-gap lab. The commands intentionally use standard tooling (cosign + openssl) but with explicit notes for HSM/USB token flows.

1) Build artifact bundle (hosted):
- Export OCI layout: skopeo copy docker://redwood/release:medisphere oci:./oci-layout/release-medisphere
- Tar and compute checksums: tar -C ./oci-layout -czf ../airgap-release-v1.tar.gz .
- sha256sum airgap-release-v1.tar.gz > airgap-release-v1.tar.gz.sha256
- release.yaml example:
  release_id: medisphere-20261010-v1
  artifacts: ["airgap-release-v1.tar.gz"]
  timestamp: 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z

2) Create detached JWS (recommended):
- Offline signer (PKCS#11 / yubikey):
  * Using pkcs11-tool + openssl for PKCS#11 HSMs:
    PKCS11_PIN=***** openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "pkcs11:token=MedHSM;id=%01" -out release.yaml.sig release.yaml
  * For YubiKey (PIV) you can use yubico-piv-tool configured for RSA-PSS.
- cosign alternative: cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key release.yaml  # only if key material can be handled per your policy
- We produce a detached JWS: release.yaml.jws (RSASSA-PSS w/ SHA-256) and include release.yaml.sig as redundancy.

3) Package for transport:
- Encrypt the tarball and signatures: openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -salt -in airgap-release-v1.tar.gz -out airgap-release-v1.tar.gz.enc -pass file:./transport_passphrase.txt
- Place artifacts on FIPS-validated USB or encrypted HDD as per Medisphere policy.

4) On-site (air-gapped) validation commands:
- Decrypt: openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -in airgap-release-v1.tar.gz.enc -out airgap-release-v1.tar.gz -pass file:./transport_passphrase.txt
- Verify checksum: sha256sum -c airgap-release-v1.tar.gz.sha256
- Verify signature (detach JWS verification using public key file): openssl dgst -sha256 -verify medisphere_release_pub.pem -signature release.yaml.sig release.yaml
- If verification passes, extract to local OCI registry: tar -C /var/lib/registry -xzf airgap-release-v1.tar.gz
- Run agent validation: redwood-agent validate --release /var/lib/registry/release-medisphere --expect-release-id medisphere-20261010-v1

5) Audit and proof of import:
- Agent returns a signed validation certificate (agent-validate-<release_id>.json) which should be stored in the Medisphere audit bucket and copies returned to Redwood for correlation.

Notes on key rotation:
- Every rotation should publish a signed rotation manifest signed by both old and new keys for a transition window. We recommend 90-day key rotation for signing keys used only for releases. See attached signing-key-rotation-rules.md.

Attachments included: airgap-artifact-bundle-v1.tar.gz (stub), signing-key-rotation-rules.md.

Let me know if you want a walkthrough video; we can run the lab pilot with your ops team Wed/Thu next week.

-Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rishi / team — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the pilot:

- Medisphere will provide a YubiKey-based signing token; can you confirm the agent supports RSA-PSS verification with the public key we share?
- For the transport passphrase: our ops team prefers a 2-of-3 split via Shamir (safed) instead of a single-file passphrase. Is that compatible with the decryption step?
- Audit evidence: please confirm the agent validation certificate includes a hash of the transport container + signature fingerprint (so our auditors can see chain-of-custody end-to-end).

If those are OK, let's schedule the pilot for Thu (2026-10-15) 10:00 PT. I'll send an invite and the contact for our courier ops.

Thanks,
Anita
Security Lead — Medisphere Health
